intro: When the Urge to Escape Arrives, with the made-up San Pedro line gone and PGQ-006 in, using both your answers. headings: # When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
### When the Urge to Escape Arrives
intro: The last h3 of Start With Whatever Showed Up. Six paragraphs now, then your Garchen Rinpoche video.

rows.label: P1, two review fixes
rows.article: Sometimes the urge to get away from what's coming up gets a lot bigger.
source: Sometimes the protective response is a sudden desire
notes: "can be progress" is the guide's word; "kind of progress" made it sound like progress in itself (stance check).

The last sentence brings back the guide's "Slow down. Bring in support when the material is bigger than your present capacity." Two reviews said that without it, a reader who just thanked the part is left alone with the drink.
Pangram alone: 100% Human (94), try 1.

carries.draft: I'd thank whatever part of you came up with the escape plan, and slow down.
carries.guide: Thank the protective part. Slow down.

carries.guide: Bring in support when the material is bigger than your present capacity.

rows.label: P2, the San Pedro fix (your account in place of the made-up line)
rows.article: So why not just blast right past that part
source: This is also why I caution against forcing your way
notes: The struck line was mine, not yours. I built it in turn 39 on My Journey's "there wasn't a grown-up me around anymore", which I'd also written myself (2026-09-16), and my review called that line yours.
Now it tells what you said happened, in your words. I left out the 7g so it can't read as a dose to copy; say if you want it in.

Question 1: did you mean your San Pedro and ayahuasca account to go in the article? Two reviewers asked. I think it works: it admits the pull of psychedelics before the caution, and "Even at a low dose, though" makes the caution about readiness, not dose. If you'd rather keep it out, I'll write P2 without it. One more thing a reviewer noticed: your "huge doses for ego death" and your 5-MeO "huge dose ... It's all spiritual bypassing" are two paragraphs apart, so a reader might link them.
"I'd hold off on psychedelics until there's enough Nurturer and Protector around": "around", not "in you", so borrowed Nurturer and Protector count, as your Altered States section says.
Pangram alone: 100% Human (106), try 1.

carries.draft: So why not just blast right past that part, with intensive meditation or psychedelics?
carries.guide: forcing your way into intensive meditation, plant medicine

carries.draft: The first time I took San Pedro cactus, at a medium-low dose, it made me super emotional, and I cried a lot.
Ayahuasca was often much more challenging, because at first I was taking huge doses for ego death.
Even at a low dose, though, I'd hold off on psychedelics until there's enough Nurturer and Protector around, and the same goes for intensive meditation.
carries.guide: before enough Nurturer and Protector capacity exists

carries.draft: Both can get you past the guards before there's a grown-up big enough to hold whatever comes through.
carries.guide: Those tools can break through protective layers faster than you can build the ability to hold what comes through.

rows.label: PGQ-006, new: your own drug history (with your paranoia answer)
rows.article: Your own drug history counts too:
source: Your own track record with psychoactive substances matters.
notes: Paranoia during a rough trip is out of the one-episode rule and has its own sentence, in your words.

Question 2: does hearing voices on a trip count as the one episode, the way the guide says? A reviewer asked, since on ayahuasca or DMT voices can be the point, as your other answer says. Your paranoia answer suggests only the kind where you lose track of what's real, or it lasts after the drug wears off. Until you say, it keeps the guide's stricter rule.
Pangram alone: 100% Human (103), try 1.

carries.draft: Your own drug history counts too: hearing voices once means no more of that drug without a professional assessment, however fine you've felt since.
carries.guide: is already enough reason not to retest that substance without professional assessment, even if you later feel stable

carries.draft: Same with badly losing your grip on reality, or your senses still being off after it wore off.
carries.guide: major loss of reality testing, or a perceptual disturbance that persists beyond the expected intoxication

carries.draft: That history matters for other drugs that mess with what's real.
carries.guide: also matters when considering other psychoactive substances that can disturb reality testing

carries.draft: I don't mean every drug's dangerous for you.
carries.guide: without turning it into a claim that every drug is dangerous for you

carries.draft: Paranoia during a rough trip is a warning sign for psychosis, so I'd reconsider the drug and dosage if trying again, as well as mindset and setting etc., and avoid ones known for causing paranoia like THC.

rows.label: PGQ-006, new: milder reactions and medicine

source.quote: Repeated milder confusion or dissociation matters too. Get prompt professional help when symptoms are severe, risky, or make safety uncertain, and especially when they persist or recur while sober. Do not abruptly stop a prescribed medicine or any substance you are physically dependent on just because it may be contributing; get appropriate medical guidance for stopping safely.

rows.label: P3, one claim cut
rows.article: Gentle meditation or self-hypnosis is a different story.
source: Gentle meditation or self-hypnosis can still help.
notes: Cut: "so the guards often ease off on their own, slowly enough for the grown-up in you to keep up". That was mine, and two stance checks found it said calming down is enough for the guards, which the article doesn't say. The guide says only that gentle versions calm the nervous system.

For your information: the stance check says the guide itself exempts gentle self-hypnosis here ("Gentle meditation or self-hypnosis can still help. My warning is about intensive versions."), while Altered States offers your self-hypnosis guide only "When you're ready". I left the wording as is.
Pangram alone: 100% Human (101), try 1.

headings: # Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
intro: Turn 40, which you haven't seen yet: the guide's first three paragraphs, as two. A candidate, waiting on one cut.

rows.label: P1, turn 40 (candidate)
rows.article: Reparenting assumes there's a clear little one in there to love
source: Reparenting assumes there is a coherent inner child to love.
notes: Pangram alone: 100% Human (73), try 3.

rows.label: P2, turn 40 (candidate), without the guide's last line
rows.article: Maybe you started playing that part so early
source: The performed self began so early
notes: The guide's "The pl/ork begins earlier, with finding or building the self." isn't in it. With that line (the proposal below), the two paragraphs and the h1 read 100% AI in four versions. Without it, both paragraphs pass together (152) and with the heading (160).

What the cut loses: the h1's opening wouldn't say outright that the work starts with finding a self. The next h2 says it ("For others, creating the conditions for it to emerge is the first phase"), so I'd cut it. Your call.

rows.label: PROPOSAL: P2 with the guide's last line (reads AI)
rows.text: Maybe you started playing that part so early, and it took over so completely, that "What do I believe?" or "What do I want?" has no clear answer of your own. They sound like such easy questions, too. Back then, asking might have gotten you in trouble, or laughed at. Or there was just no way to ask. That can make "love yourself" feel pretty empty (love what, when the part you've been playing doesn't feel real?). For you, then, the pl/ork starts a step earlier, with finding a self or building one, which can take a while.
rows.proposal_of: Maybe you started playing that part so early
